title: Students’ voices on generative AI: perceptions, benefits, and challenges in higher education
venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education
extended_summary:
This paper examines university students’ perceptions of generative AI (GenAI), especially tools such as ChatGPT, in higher education. The authors focus on how familiar students are with GenAI, what benefits they expect from it, what concerns they have, and how it might be integrated responsibly into teaching and learning. The study is framed around the idea that student perceptions shape uptake and learning outcomes, and it responds to the rapid rise of GenAI in higher education.

The study used an online survey with both closed-ended and open-ended questions, administered to 399 undergraduate and postgraduate students from six universities in Hong Kong. Quantitative analysis assessed students’ knowledge of GenAI, willingness to use it, and concerns about it, while thematic analysis of open responses explored perceived benefits and risks in more depth. The context was general higher education use, not a specific classroom intervention or coaching system.

Findings suggest that students generally view GenAI positively and see value in personalized learning support, writing and brainstorming help, research assistance, multimedia creation, and administrative efficiency. At the same time, they express substantial concerns about accuracy, transparency, privacy, plagiarism, over-reliance, effects on creativity and critical thinking, career displacement, and unclear institutional policies. The paper concludes that GenAI can support higher education, but effective implementation requires AI literacy, ethical guidance, privacy protections, transparency, and institutional safeguards.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI conversational large language model chatbot that generates human-like text responses to prompts and can assist with writing, feedback, brainstorming, and question answering.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper discusses ChatGPT as an example of generative AI in higher education and reports students’ perceptions of using it for personalized learning support, writing and brainstorming, research support, and administrative tasks. It is not evaluated as a formal intervention in a school coaching system.

findings.finding_summary: Students reported a generally positive attitude toward using ChatGPT-like generative AI in higher education. In the survey of 399 undergraduate and postgraduate students in Hong Kong, perceived benefits included personalized and immediate learning support, writing feedback, research assistance, and 24/7 anonymous support; concerns remained about accuracy, privacy, ethics, over-reliance, and uncertain policies.
findings.measure: Survey responses on willingness to use generative AI, perceived benefits, and concerns

quality_tier_rationale: This is a cross-sectional survey with open-ended responses, so it provides useful descriptive evidence but not causal impact evidence. The paper studies perceptions and policy implications rather than testing an intervention.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports positive perceived usefulness but no measured learning effect sizes or outcome gains. Its impact is therefore suggestive and indirect rather than demonstrated through effect estimates.
